info.title: AgentBase Memory API
info.description:
Managed long-term memory service for AI agents. It captures the raw events of an agent's interactions and distills them into durable, semantically searchable memory records, so your agents can recall context across sessions without you running your own vector store or extraction pipeline.

## Authentication
Every request must carry a VNG Cloud IAM OAuth2 access token in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <access_token>`. Use the **Authorize** button above to set it for "Try it out" calls. The gateway validates the token and enforces fine-grained IAM permissions on the **Agent Memory** resource.

## Core concepts
- **Memory**: a top-level store you own. It holds the events and memory records for one agent application, and defines how long raw events are retained (`eventExpiryDuration`, in days) and which long-term memory strategies apply.
- **Long-term memory strategy (LTMS)**: the recipe for turning raw interactions into long-term memory records. It sets the extraction `type`, an optional custom fact-extraction prompt, a `namespaceTemplate` that decides where records land, and whether records are generated automatically.
- **Event**: an immutable raw interaction (a payload plus timestamp) appended under an actor and session. Events form the short-term, episodic history and expire after the memory's `eventExpiryDuration`.
- **Actor / Session**: events are organized by **actor** (who the interaction is with, e.g. an end user) and **session** (a single conversation with that actor).
- **Memory record**: a distilled long-term fact extracted from events or supplied content. Records live in a **namespace** and are retrievable by semantic search.
- **Namespace**: a logical partition for memory records, resolved from a strategy's `namespaceTemplate` (which may contain placeholders such as `{actorId}`).

Records can be produced automatically as events accumulate, generated on demand from a session or from content you post, or inserted directly.

get.description: Streams the events of an actor's session as JSON, most recent first, optionally bounded by the `fromTimestamp`/`toTimestamp` range. Page size is capped at 100.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the memory store, as returned by `POST /memories`.

parameters.name: actorId
parameters.description: Id of the actor, the participant the events belong to, typically a user id or an agent id. Chosen by the caller.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Id of the session, one coherent conversation thread for the actor. Chosen by the caller. A `;` cannot be carried in a path segment, where it starts a matrix parameter, so a session id that contains one, as a Microsoft Teams conversation id does, has to be mapped onto the accepted character set before it is sent. Percent-encoding it as `%3B` does not help.

parameters.name: fromTimestamp
parameters.description: Return only events at or after this instant, as an ISO-8601 instant in UTC. Defaults to the start of the event retention window of the memory, and is clamped to it: events older than `eventExpiryDuration` days are never returned.

parameters.name: toTimestamp
parameters.description: Return only events at or before this instant, as an ISO-8601 instant in UTC. Unbounded when omitted.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return. 1-based.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of items per page. Between 1 and 100.

name.description: Name of the strategy, for the caller to recognise it by.

type.description: Which kind of facts to extract. Has to be one of the built-in strategy types: `USER_PREFERENCES` for the preferences, habits and traits of the user, `SEMANTIC` for general factual statements, or `CUSTOM` to drive extraction with your own `customFactExtractionPrompt` instead.

customFactExtractionPrompt.description: Your own fact extraction instructions, used in place of the built-in prompt. Only meaningful when `type` is `CUSTOM`.
customFactExtractionPrompt.example: Extract only facts related to the user's technical stack and project requirements.

namespaceTemplate.description: Where the extracted memory records are stored, as a template. The placeholders `{memoryStrategyId}`, `{actorId}` and `{sessionId}` are substituted at extraction time, and the resolved string is the `namespace` to pass when listing or searching records. Choosing which placeholders to include is what scopes the records: `{actorId}` alone makes them shared across all of that actor's sessions, adding `{sessionId}` confines them to one session.

enableAutomaticMemoryRecordGeneration.description: Whether a background job runs this strategy over new events on its own schedule. When false, records are only extracted when you call one of the `memory-records:generate-from-...` endpoints.

name.description: Name of the memory store, for the caller to recognise it by.

description.description: What this memory store is for. May be empty, but has to be present.
description.example: Memory for my customer support chatbot

eventExpiryDuration.description: How many days raw events are retained, between 1 and 365. Events older than this are left out of event listings and are deleted by a background job. Memory records extracted from them are not affected.

longTermMemoryStrategies.description: The long-term memory strategies to attach to this memory, at most 10. Each one governs what kind of facts are extracted from the events and which namespace the resulting memory records are stored under. Two strategies of the same `type` cannot be attached to the same memory.

id.description: Id of the memory store, generated by the service. Pass it as the `{id}` path segment of every other endpoint.

name.description: Name given to the memory store when it was created.

description.description: Description given to the memory store when it was created. May be empty.
description.example: Memory for my customer support chatbot

eventExpiryDuration.description: How many days raw events are retained. Events older than this are left out of event listings and are deleted by a background job.

portalUserId.description: Id of the portal user that owns this memory store, resolved from the credentials of the request.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the memory store. Always `ACTIVE`: deleted memories are never returned.

createdAt.description: When the memory store was created.

updatedAt.description: When the memory store was last modified.

query.description: What to search for. Matching is by semantic similarity rather than keyword, so phrase this as the question the agent needs answered.
query.example: What are this user's UI preferences?

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return, between 5 and 200.

scoreThreshold.description: Minimum similarity score a record has to reach to be returned, between 0 and 1. Defaults to 0, which returns the `limit` closest records however weak the match. Raise it to trade recall for precision.

id.description: Id of the memory record. Pass it as the `{memoryRecordId}` path segment to delete this record.

memory.description: The fact itself, as a self-contained sentence. This is the text to inject into the prompt of your agent.

score.description: How closely this record matches the search query, between 0 and 1, higher being closer. Only set for search results, since listing records does not rank them.

created_at.description: When the memory record was extracted.

updated_at.description: When the memory record was last revised. The extraction pipeline updates an existing record in place when a later conversation refines the same fact.

memoryRecords.description: The facts to store, at most 100, each a self-contained sentence as the extraction pipeline would have produced. They are stored verbatim under the given namespace and are searchable straight away.

content.example: I prefer dark mode and short answers.

chatMessages.description: The conversation to extract facts from, at most 100 messages, in chronological order. These are read for extraction only and are not stored as events, so they will not appear in event listings afterwards.

payload.description: The content of the event. Which fields apply depends on `payload.type`.

eventTimestamp.description: When the interaction happened, as an ISO-8601 instant in UTC. Defaults to the time the request is received. Set it explicitly when replaying or backfilling a conversation, since this is the timestamp events are ordered, filtered and expired by.

type.description: What kind of event this is. `conversational` for a text turn, which requires `role` and `message`, or `binary` for arbitrary content, which requires `binaryData`. Only long-term memory strategies read conversational events, so binary events are stored and returned but never contribute to memory records.

role.description: Who produced the message: `user`, `assistant` or `system`. Required when `type` is `conversational`, and ignored otherwise.

message.description: The text of the turn. Required when `type` is `conversational`, and ignored otherwise.
message.example: I prefer dark mode and short answers.

binaryData.description: Arbitrary content, base64-encoded. Required when `type` is `binary`, and ignored otherwise.

listData.description: The items on this page. Empty when the requested page is past the end of the results.

page.description: The page these items came from, echoing the `page` request parameter. 1-based.

pageSize.description: The page size these items were read with, echoing the `size` request parameter.

totalPage.description: Total number of pages at this page size.

totalItem.description: Total number of items across all pages.
